respect.say: respect for someone · show respect · treat with respect
ex: Children should show respect to their teachers.
I have a lot of respect for my doctor.
Please treat everyone at work with respect.
She earned the respect of her whole team.
respect.note: Also a verb: "I respect my parents."

laptop.say: on my laptop · work on a laptop

policeman.say: ask a policeman · call the police
ex: Excuse me, where can I find a policeman?
A policeman helped me find the train station.
My uncle works as a policeman in Kyiv.
The policeman asked to see my driver's license.
policeman.note: "Police officer" is more common and neutral today.

snack.say: have a snack · a healthy snack
ex: I usually eat a small snack after work.
Apples and nuts make a healthy snack.
Can we buy some snacks for the trip?
The kids want a snack after school.
The doctor asked about the pain in his penis.
The penis is part of the male body.
Wash a baby boy's penis gently with warm water.
He went to a doctor about a problem with his penis.

conflict.say: a conflict between · in conflict with · avoid conflict

ex: Cats catch mice by instinct, not by learning.
My first instinct was to call my mom.
Trust your instincts when you choose a new job.
A mother's instinct is to protect her baby.

plastic.say: made of plastic · a plastic bag
plastic.note: Often used before nouns: a plastic bag, a plastic bottle.

ex: I'd like my steak medium rare, please.
How would you like your steak cooked?
This restaurant serves the best steak in town.
We often have steak and potatoes on Sunday.
Can I have tea with lemon, please?
Squeeze some lemon juice over the fish.
These lemons are very sour and juicy.
I need two lemons for this cake.

ritual.say: a daily ritual · a morning ritual
ex: Morning coffee is my favorite daily ritual.
Reading a story before bed is our family ritual.
Lighting candles is part of the wedding ritual.
Every sports team has its own little rituals.

acre.note: One acre is about 4,047 square meters (0.4 hectares).

calendar.say: on the calendar · in my calendar

ex: Gambling is not allowed in this city.
He lost all his money on online gambling.
Gambling can become a serious problem for families.
Is gambling legal in your country?
gambling.note: Uncountable: "gambling," not "a gambling." The verb is "gamble."

ex: The doctor used a laser to fix her eyes.
My cat chases the red laser on the floor.
The machine uses a laser to cut metal.
Can I print this on the laser printer?

peak.say: at its peak · peak hours · reach the peak
ex: We reached the peak of the mountain by noon.
The view from the peak is amazing.
Snow covers the mountain peaks all year.
Avoid the subway at peak hours; it is very crowded.
peak.note: Do not confuse with "peek" (a quick look).

parade.say: watch a parade · in the parade
ex: The whole town watched the parade on the main street.
Soldiers marched in the parade on Independence Day.
We can see the parade from our balcony.
What time does the parade start tomorrow?
What are the ingredients in this cake?
Fresh ingredients make the food taste better.
Flour is the main ingredient in bread.
Can you buy the ingredients for dinner tonight?

fiction.say: science fiction · read fiction · a work of fiction
ex: She reads fiction more than history books.
The fiction section is on the second floor.
He writes science fiction for young readers.
Do you prefer fiction or true stories?
fiction.note: Uncountable: a work of fiction (not "a fiction").

mechanism.say: a mechanism for · a safety mechanism
ex: The lock has a simple mechanism inside.
The mechanism in this old clock still works.
Can you fix the mechanism of this door?
This toy uses a spring mechanism to jump.

radar.say: on the radar · a radar screen

ex: LOL, your photo of the cat is so funny!
LOL, I fell asleep in class again today.
She texted me "LOL" after my silly joke.
LOL, that is the best video I've seen.
LOL.note: Used in chats and texts. It means "laughing out loud."

cream.say: put cream on · hand cream · face cream
ex: Put some cream on your hands every night.
Do you have a cream for dry skin?
This cream helps with sunburn and red skin.
I need a good face cream for winter.
cream.note: Most often "cream" is the thick part of milk: "coffee with cream."

cargo.note: Usually uncountable: some cargo, a lot of cargo.

ex: The audio is too quiet, can you turn it up?
I can't hear the audio on this video.
Please check your audio before the online meeting.
You can download the audio file for this lesson.

essay.say: write an essay · an essay about
ex: I have to write an essay for English class.
Her essay about her family won first prize.
The essay is due next Monday morning.
Can you check my essay for mistakes, please?

sensor.say: a motion sensor · a fingerprint sensor

gender.note: In grammar, "gender" also means masculine or feminine words.

DJ.say: hire a DJ · the DJ at a party

lifestyle.say: a healthy lifestyle · change your lifestyle
ex: Doctors say a healthy lifestyle is very important.
Moving to the city changed his whole lifestyle.
She writes a blog about food and lifestyle.
A busy lifestyle can cause a lot of stress.

bacon.say: bacon and eggs · a slice of bacon
ex: I usually have bacon and eggs for breakfast.
Can I get extra bacon on my sandwich?
The whole kitchen smells like fried bacon.
Add some crispy bacon to the salad.
bacon.note: Uncountable: some bacon, a slice of bacon (not "a bacon").

ex: We paid an internet consultant to build our online store.
An internet consultant helps companies sell more online.
She works as an internet consultant for small businesses.
Our internet consultant said we need a better website.
internet consultant.note: Rare. For help in a website chat, English says "online support" or "live chat."

original.note: Most often "original" is an adjective meaning first: "the original plan."

deposit.say: make a deposit · a bank deposit
ex: I want to make a deposit, please.
My bank pays good interest on a deposit.
Can I make a deposit at this ATM?
She keeps her savings in a bank deposit.
deposit.note: Often "deposit" is money you pay first: "a deposit for the apartment."

pulse.say: check your pulse · take someone's pulse
ex: The nurse checked my pulse and blood pressure.
You can feel your pulse on your wrist.
His pulse was very fast after the run.
Let me take your pulse for one minute.
The admiral visited the sailors on the ship.
An admiral is a very high rank in the navy.
Her grandfather was an admiral in the navy.
The admiral gave orders to all the ships.

cafe.say: at a cafe · in a cafe
ex: Let's meet at the cafe on the corner.
She works part-time in a small cafe.
Is there a good cafe near the station?
This cafe has great cakes and coffee.

mister.gram: mister · as a title: Mr. Smith
mister.note: Usually written "Mr." before a name; "mister" alone is informal.

ex: They need more capital to start the business.
He used his own capital to open the shop.
The company got capital from three investors.
How much capital do you need for a cafe?
capital.note: Most often "capital" means the main city: "Kyiv is the capital of Ukraine."

release.say: a new release · a press release
release.note: Most often "release" means to let go or free: "They released him from prison."

image.note: Most often "image" means a picture: "Click on the image to see it bigger."

rhythm.say: to the rhythm · a sense of rhythm
ex: This song has a great rhythm for dancing.
Clap your hands to the rhythm of the music.
I have no sense of rhythm at all.
The drummer keeps the rhythm for the band.

workshop.say: a workshop on · go to a workshop
ex: I signed up for a free writing workshop.
The workshop lasts two days and costs fifty dollars.
She runs a workshop on public speaking.
Are you going to the photo workshop on Saturday?
workshop.note: Also a room where people make or fix things: "my dad's workshop."

guide.say: a tour guide · a local guide
guide.note: Often "guide" is a book or text that helps: "a travel guide to Kyiv."

collapse.say: the collapse of · close to collapse
ex: The economy is close to collapse after the war.
Many people lost their jobs after the bank's collapse.
The collapse of the company shocked its workers.
The hospital system is near collapse.
collapse.note: Most often "collapse" is a verb, fall down: "The old bridge collapsed."

immigrant.say: an immigrant from · come as an immigrant
ex: My grandparents came here as immigrants.
Many immigrants live and work in this city.
She helps new immigrants find jobs and homes.
Are you an immigrant or were you born here?
Small boats travel along the canal every day.
We walked along the old canal after lunch.
The city has many canals and small bridges.
Can we take a boat tour on the canal?
canal.note: A TV channel is a "channel," not a "canal."

ex: Police say a hired killer shot the businessman.
The movie is about a paid killer in Paris.
He worked as a hired killer for a gang.
The hired killer was caught at the airport.
killer.note: Most often "killer" is any person who kills. A paid killer is a "hit man."

ex: Kids at school called him a freak.
I'm not a freak, I just like different music.
They looked at me like I was a freak.
Don't call people freaks, it's very rude.
freak.note: Often in "freak out": get very upset or scared. Calling someone a freak is rude.

agenda.say: on the agenda · a hidden agenda
ex: The new party has a clear political agenda.
Health care is high on the government's agenda.
I think he has a hidden agenda.
Climate change is on every party's agenda now.
agenda.note: Also a list of topics for a meeting: "What is on the agenda today?"

luxury.say: a luxury hotel · live in luxury
luxury.note: Often used before nouns: a luxury hotel, a luxury car.

cocktail.say: order a cocktail · a cocktail party
ex: We ordered two cocktails at the hotel bar.
This cocktail has lime, mint, and ice.
What is your favorite cocktail to order?
Can I see the cocktail menu, please?
cocktail.note: A milk drink is a "milkshake," not a "cocktail."

ex: Heh, that is a really funny joke.
Heh, I didn't think you would notice.
He just said "heh" and smiled at me.
Heh, nice try, but I know the answer.
heh.note: Informal, mostly in writing and chat.

container.say: a plastic container · a container of
ex: Put the leftovers in a plastic container.
The ship carries hundreds of big containers.
Keep the cookies in a container with a lid.
Do you have a container for this soup?

arena.say: at the arena · in the arena

ex: The officer carried a pistol on his belt.
He cleaned his pistol after shooting practice.
The police found a pistol in the car.
You need a license to own a pistol here.
pistol.note: "Gun" is the more common everyday word.
